questions.question: How did people write before typewriters, and what problems did this cause?
questions.expected_answer: They wrote by hand with quill pens, dip pens with nibs and ink, fountain pens and pencils. It was slow, ink could smudge and blot, handwriting could be hard to read, and clerks had to copy every document by hand to make copies.

questions.question: Who invented the typewriter, and how does a manual typewriter work?
questions.expected_answer: Christopher Latham Sholes and his partners patented a typewriter in 1868, sold by Remington from 1874. When you press a key, a lever swings up a metal typebar with a raised letter, which hits an ink ribbon against the paper and prints the letter. The carriage moves one space, a bell rings near the end of a line, and the carriage return lever starts a new line. It needs no electricity.

questions.question: Give three ways typewriters changed people's lives.
questions.expected_answer: Writing became faster, neater and easier to read; offices, governments, newspapers and schools could produce documents quickly; many women got jobs as typists and secretaries; writers could type their books. The QWERTY keyboard is still used on computers and phones today.
